title: DR1 asks for a microchip number when identifying horses, cats and dogs; the frontend never asks for one

finding.frontend: Identifying a horse offers two boxes, Passport number and Horse name, and nothing else — that is the whole entry form on fe-animal-identification-horse. Cats and dogs get Passport number and Tattoo. No screen in the service asks for a microchip number, and no field exists for one: the identifier set is fixed at six obligations in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198 — passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, identification details, description — with the labels in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-79. The only occurrence of the word microchip in the whole application is a test fixture typing "Microchip 900123" into the free-text identification-details box.
finding.prototype: DR1 defines a microchip as an identifier on two commodity codes in app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-20 — 0101 (Horse), where the set is Microchip, Passport, Horse name, and 01061900 (Cat, Dog, Ferret, Other live mammals), where the set is Microchip, Passport, Tattoo. It is the first field in both sets, so on the identification page a horse, cat or dog line opens with a Microchip box above the others. No DR1 capture shows it: the corpus's only DR1 identification screenshot is a cattle line, and 0102 has no microchip.
finding.difference: Add a microchip identifier to the six-obligation identifier set: a new obligation in identifiers.js allow-listed to Horse, Cat and Dog, its label and hint in the commodities copy file, and its inclusion in the free-text fallback's inverse gate so a microchip commodity stops falling through to Identification details. DR1 places it first in the horse and cat/dog sets, so the field order changes too. Nothing blocks this in the frontend, but the value has to reach the notification payload, so check the identifier mapping in src/server/app/services/persistence/records/notification-mapper/ carries a sixth identifier before the field is added.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a microchip input rendered on any frontend identification screen, or any commodity whose scoped field list in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/fields.js:27-30 resolves to a microchip field.
finding.verification: Opened fe-animal-identification-horse (Passport number and Horse name only) and dr1-animal-identification-details, which is a cattle panel, so DR1's horse and cat/dog panels are unphotographed in this corpus. Read app/data/commodity-identifiers.js whole — microchip is the first entry on 0101 and on 01061900 and appears on no other code — and on the frontend side identifiers.js:113-198 and copy.en.js:58-79. Ran the falsifier: scopedFields at identifier/fields.js:27-30 draws only from copy.typeFields and copy.fallbackFields, neither of which holds a microchip, and grepping the whole of src/ for "microchip" returns three fixture lines and nothing else. Corroborated by the repo's own render matrix at animal-identification.controller.test.js:364-406, which pins Horse to passport and horseName and Cat and Dog to passport and tattoo. CORRECT, with confidence lowered — see correction.
finding.correction: Claimed confidence high. The frontend half is observable — five captures plus an exhaustive grep of src/ — but DR1's microchip box appears in no picture and no rendered DOM in this corpus, because the only DR1 identification capture is a cattle line and 0102 has no microchip. Against the contract's bar, where high means the claim is observable in the pictures or the rendered HTML, that makes this medium. Confidence is lowered and the unphotographed state is now named in finding.prototype. The claim itself is unchanged and holds: app/data/commodity-identifiers.js gives 0101 microchip, passport, horse-name and 01061900 microchip, passport, tattoo, microchip first in both.
